bullets.title: Nasdaq hits intraday ATH; AI-tech rotation out of financials drives tape
bullets.body: The Nasdaq 100 extended gains 0.6% and reached a new intraday all-time high, with AI-linked tech stocks leading a rotation out of financials. The Dow fell 0.5% and the S&P 500 was flat-to-modestly-positive; bank stocks slid amid renewed fears of AI-agent disintermediation. GS desk flagged subdued activity (3/10) with LOs and HFs net sellers, and a noticeable increase in software shorts.

bullets.title: Fed Barkin and Collins strike hawkish tone; 50/50 odds of another hike next month
bullets.body: Fed's Barkin stated last week's hike was justified because inflation risks outweigh employment risks and hopes the period resembles the 1990s mid-cycle adjustment, but cautioned the Fed cannot assume markets will keep rates high enough. Collins separately said she now sees an increased likelihood of inflation staying 'notably above 2%' and backed a 'somewhat more restrictive' federal funds rate. Markets are pricing a 50/50 chance of another hike next month.

bullets.title: 2Y Treasury auction tails; yields hit 3-year-plus highs as foreign demand slides
bullets.body: The 2-year Treasury auction priced at 4.787%, a 0.2bp tail to the 4.785% when-issued level, with foreign demand declining — the highest yield in over three years. The 10s-2s spread widened 19bps to a new cycle low and the 2s-30s curve compressed to just below 55bps, having halved in about a month. A paper flagged that 90% of the 10-year yield rise since August 2020 has occurred in three-day windows around Fed events.

bullets.title: Richmond Fed data misses badly; non-manufacturing index collapses to -22
bullets.body: September Richmond Fed Manufacturing Index came in at -2 versus the +2 estimate and +4 prior, while the non-manufacturing index plunged to -22.0 versus -8.7 expected and -10.6 prior — a sharp deterioration in services activity. Prices paid in Philadelphia Fed services jumped to +37.8 from +29.2, reinforcing the inflation-remains-sticky narrative.

bullets.title: Oil down 6 straight days; Brent breaks below $100 on Iran strait reopening signals
bullets.body: Crude oil is on track for six consecutive down days, its longest streak since August 2025, with Brent falling below $100/barrel on a Kyodo report that Iran may be willing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Trump separately said oil prices 'will plummet' after the Iran conflict ends and that more oil is flowing than at any point since the war started. Simultaneously, Saudi Arabia restarted its East-West pipeline and signaled Red Sea loadings to Asia could soon resume, while gulf-to-China shipping costs hit a record $1M/day.

bullets.title: Trump endorses diesel export ban; Bessent examining feasibility as prices hit $6.53
bullets.body: Trump backed calls for a moratorium on US diesel exports ('I've called for that too'), with Treasury Secretary Bessent confirming the administration is examining whether a ban is feasible. Diesel prices rose to $6.53; Trump advisers tied higher gas prices to strained refining capacity from strikes on Russian refineries. Alaska Sen. Sullivan also separately called for a moratorium. WTI crack spreads hit a new all-time high.

bullets.title: SPY options flow bullish: $11B dark pool print and $2.8B call wall at 775
bullets.body: An $11B dark pool print in SPY at 662.69 — one of only two such prints this year — is being read as a bullish signal. There is also a $2.8B call wall at the 775 strike that bulls need to clear to extend the squeeze. A $3M OTM SPY put purchase is the only counter-signal but was described as not yet actionable.

bullets.title: US money supply grew 5.7% YoY — largest increase since June 2022
bullets.body: US money supply expanded 5.7% year-over-year, the largest increase since June 2022, resuming monetary expansion after a brief pause. Howard Marks echoed Druckenmiller in warning that Treasury buybacks amid sticky inflation and large deficits pose a fiscal risk and could pressure the US dollar, and called the situation 'a problem with US fiscal management.'

bullets.title: META surges 32.7% MTD — strongest month since 2013 — on Muse AI launch
bullets.body: META gained roughly +32.7% this month, its strongest performance since 2013, driven by the launch of its Muse AI app and a partnership with Shopify (SHOP +7.3%). Multiple observers note META's fixed-strike volatility is compressing today (bearish for long calls), while one hedge warned META could announce a secondary offering that caps momentum. Retail bulls are speculating on a $1,000+ year-end price target.

bullets.title: Alibaba unveils $53B 'most powerful' China AI chip (Zhenwu V900), 10T-parameter model
bullets.body: Alibaba launched the Zhenwu V900 processor — claimed as the most powerful AI chip in the market — in a $53B strategic investment push, alongside a 10-trillion-parameter model at its Apsara conference. Clusters of 500,000 V900 GPUs are planned. BABA ADRs gained 3% in premarket on the news.

bullets.title: Bessent frontrunner for Trump 'AI Czar' role; US rejects globalist AI control scheme
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent is reported as the frontrunner for a new White House 'AI czar' position, and is said to have reservations about Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. Trump separately declared at the UN that the US 'will not stifle growth' of AI (which he wants to rename 'Super Intelligence'), calling it potentially larger than the Industrial Revolution, while rejecting any globalist AI control frameworks.

bullets.title: Anthropic cuts Claude Opus 5.5 pricing 40%; Box sees 63% token reduction
bullets.body: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 priced at $4/$20 per million input/output tokens — roughly 40% cheaper than Opus 5 — while delivering comparable performance to Fable 5.1 on most tasks. Box's enterprise testing found 63% fewer tokens used and a 42% performance improvement versus Opus 5. The release precedes a rumored Anthropic IPO.

bullets.title: Texas Governor halts new data centers; moratoriums covering 20 GW of capacity
bullets.body: Texas Governor ordered a halt to new data center construction weeks after issuing a moratorium. Across all US jurisdictions, 400+ local actions have been tracked, with 300+ moratoriums enacted covering 20 GW of capacity — though only 1.5 GW is estimated to face actual delays since 6.7 GW already holds permits and significant capacity is outside effective reach. Developers with existing permits and credible power timelines gain competitive advantage.

bullets.title: AWS wins first-ever NATO Restricted cloud certification
bullets.body: AWS received NATO Restricted cloud approval, clearing it to handle NR-level defense workloads across all NATO member nations — the first cloud provider to achieve this certification level. No other tracked cloud names were mentioned as competing for the same designation.

bullets.title: Trump-Xi summit expected light on deals; Xi unlikely to bring Chinese CEOs
bullets.body: Multiple sources report Xi Jinping will not bring a delegation of Chinese corporate executives to the Washington meeting with Trump, and the summit is expected to focus on extending the trade truce rather than major agreements — a signal to temper expectations for near-term US-China bilateral business activity.

bullets.title: S&P breadth diverging: 43% of members oversold while index sits overbought
bullets.body: Despite the S&P 500 returning to overbought territory on price, 43% of index constituents are oversold and only 11% are overbought — a significant breadth divergence that strategists warn historically precedes deteriorating market participation and eventual underperformance, even if a near-term tech-led rally to new highs remains the base case.

bullets.title: Grok 4.7 launches in Tesla vehicles; SpaceX AI Grok bot hits 400K users with 24% weekly growth
bullets.body: Grok Bot officially launched in Tesla vehicles, enabling complex task automation including ordering and scheduling. Separately, SpaceX AI's Grok bot agent surpassed 400,000 users after its first month with 24% week-over-week user growth. Grok 4.7 Fast is also now live in Grok Build and Cursor.

bullets.title: Trump discloses 1,156 July trades including up to $25M each of MSFT and AMZN sold
bullets.body: Trump filed a periodic transaction report covering 1,156 securities trades in July totaling at least $270M in activity, including sales of up to $25M each of Microsoft and Amazon on July 20. Total purchases in July reached at least $43.6M versus at least $35.6M in sales. Palantir was identified as a stock being actively day-traded in the portfolio.

bullets.title: Eurozone consumer confidence misses; UK August borrowing hits £18.3B, above consensus
bullets.body: Eurozone consumer confidence fell to -16.5 in September versus -16.0 expected and -15.5 prior, signaling weakening economic sentiment in the bloc. UK public sector borrowing reached £18.3B in August, exceeding the £15.5B consensus, driven by higher debt servicing costs and inflation — adding pressure ahead of next month's budget announcement.

bullets.title: Bitcoin jumps 13% in a week; ETF inflows hit $1B as $108K price target emerges
bullets.body: Bitcoin rose 13% over the past week to $86,000 with a $1B+ ETF inflow triggering a technical breakout; prediction markets on Polymarket show a 42% probability of Bitcoin reaching $100,000 by year-end. The $108K level has been flagged as the next technical target. Cryptocurrency ownership among investors has meanwhile dropped to 11% from 17% in 2025 per Gallup.
